Governor Ivey Announces Longtime Chief of Staff Liz Filmore to Depart

November 17, 2026

Press Releases

Share

MONTGOMERY –
 Governor Kay Ivey on Tuesday announced her longtime chief of staff, Liz Filmore, will depart the Governor’s Office Tuesday, December 1. Filmore is Governor Ivey’s longest serving chief of staff, as well as her longest serving staff member.

“Liz has been a very, very effective chief of staff these last five years, and Alabama is better thanks to her service,” 
said Governor Ivey.
 “She will be noted as the first female chief of staff to any Alabama governor, but she will be remembered for what she did with that opportunity. Together, we have accomplished a lot for our state. She has truly motivated each staff member and cabinet officer. After everything is said and done, I believe she will be known as my best chief of staff. I wish her the best in her next opportunity and have all the confidence in the world she will continue serving Alabama well!”

The governor tapped Filmore to serve as chief of staff five years ago on December 1, 2021. Prior to stepping into the chief of staff role, Filmore served on the governor’s staff and had been a close confidante and advisor to the governor since Governor Ivey’s reelection campaign for lieutenant governor in 2013.

“It has been the honor of my life to serve with Governor Kay Ivey over the past 13 years and to lead her team for the last five years,” 
said Filmore.
 “Her example, expectation of perfection, vision, confidence and encouragement has molded my career and who I am today. I am grateful to Governor Ivey for seeing my potential and allowing me to serve as the first woman chief of staff to an Alabama governor.”

Shortly after Filmore assumed the helm as chief of staff, the people of Alabama overwhelmingly elected Governor Ivey to a second full term. The governor defeated eight opponents in the Primary Election with no runoff and won the General Election with 67 percent of the vote.

During the governor’s inaugural address, she stated that the Administration would have a “busy, productive and full four years” and Filmore certainly was a key force behind that promise being fulfilled. In the same remarks, Governor Ivey laid out the bold goal of having Alabama rank in the top 30 states for reading and math for the first time in the state’s history. Once again, Filmore helped to see that into reality. Filmore has been a part of the governor’s record job creation, as well as at the forefront of pushing hallmark legislation across the finish line. From maintaining competitive economic incentives to the creation of the CHOOSE Act education savings accounts to establishing Alabama’s first public residential high school dedicated to healthcare education, Filmore has helped Governor Ivey execute her ambitious legislative plans. Those efforts also included paid parental leave for teachers, a comprehensive Safe Alabama public safety package of bills, fully funding a statewide notification system, the FOCUS Act and limiting screen time among the state’s youngest learners. Filmore also worked closely with Governor Ivey and the Finance Director to usher the state’s budgets through the legislative process, including the largest ever Education Trust Fund.

“I am incredibly thankful and proud of the team’s integrity, as well as the professionalism demonstrated by the cabinet and staff who have worked diligently to move Alabama forward. Governor Ivey is a transformative leader, and I am honored to have had a front row seat to witness her work for all Alabamians,” 
concluded Filmore.

As chief, Filmore works with Governor Ivey to oversee the 23 state agencies with over 20,000 employees, in addition to managing the staff in the Governor’s Office.

Upon Filmore’s departure December 1, Governor Ivey’s deputy chief of staff, Nathan Lindsay, will assume the position for the remainder of the term. Lindsay has been with the Ivey Administration since July 2019.

An official photo of Liz Filmore is attached.
